headline: Tech-led stock rout sends 10Y CCDC 1.7bp lower to 1.587%; 20–30Y lead as curve bull-flattens
summary: CGBs rallied and bull-flattened as A-shares slumped. The CCDC 10-year fell 1.7bp to 1.587%, a fresh 1-year low (the on-the-run 260016 traded at a record low near 1.57%), and the 30-year 1.5bp to 2.027%, with the 20-year down 1.9bp leading while the 2-year slipped only 0.6bp to 1.216%; over the week the 10-year is down 6.3bp. Policy banks lagged at 5–10Y: CDB, ADBC and EXIM 10-year each fell 1.2bp, to 1.636%, 1.669% and 1.660%, so the CDB 10-year spread widened 0.5bp to 4.9bp, while EXIM 2-year fell 2bp and long policy bank bonds tracked CGBs one for one.
drivers: The Shanghai Composite fell 1.1% to 3,649 and ChiNext 4.0% as AI hardware and optical-module names sold off, with turnover down about RMB460bn to roughly RMB1.66tn. The long end rallied hardest in the afternoon: TL futures rose 0.41% and T 0.10%, while 20–30Y CCDC yields fell 1.5–1.9bp.
Anchor shift keeps funding cheap, but front end stalls

The PBOC ran RMB226bn of overnight reverse repos at 1.25% against RMB278bn maturing, a fifth straight daily net drain (RMB52bn), and overnight Shibor rose 2bp to 1.283% and 7-day 2.3bp to 1.346%. With funding already priced near the 1.25% anchor, the 2-year fell only 0.6bp and TS futures were flat; Governor Pan's report to the NPC Standing Committee kept the moderately loose stance, and the PBOC's net CGB buying of RMB150bn in October was its largest this year.

The MoF sold 1-year bills at a 1.1403% average with about 3.1 times cover and 50-year bonds at 2.1537% with about 7.1 times cover, in line with the 2.152% CCDC 50-year. EXIM's 1-year tap cleared at 1.2683% with 3 times cover, helping its 2-year fall 2bp.
Global yields lower, yuan held back

US 10-year Treasuries fell about 5bp to 4.84% on Thursday, and the PBOC set a fixing about 400 pips weaker than expected, leaving the yuan near 6.67 and on track for its first weekly loss in six weeks. A softer yuan removes some of the pressure from the recent FX RRR hike without constraining domestic easing.
data: Oct RatingDog services PMI (Nov 4)
50.8 (f 51.5, p 51.6); composite 52.0 (p 52.4); selling prices cut for a 2nd month
Slowest services growth since July with falling prices supports low yields, though bonds sold off later on equities.
Oct RatingDog mfg PMI (Nov 2)
52.0 (f 51.6, p 52.1); output fastest since April; 11th month of expansion
Private and export-facing firms are holding up, which tempers the weak official print but did not stop the bond rally.
Oct official PMIs (Oct 31)
Mfg 49.3 (f 50.0, p 50.1); new orders 49.4; non-mfg 49.7 (p 50.2); composite 49.7
Back in contraction with softer prices, which supports low yields and the case for continued easy funding.
Q3 PBOC loan report (Oct 28)
Property loans RMB50.08tn, −5.2% y/y; mortgages RMB35.91tn, −4.1% y/y (−1.1tn YTD)
Households keep paying down mortgages, so credit demand stays weak and banks keep buying bonds.
Sep industrial profits (Oct 27)
A beat driven by AI hardware, metals and oil-linked prices, not households; bonds looked through it.
Oct MLF (Oct 26)
RMB700bn 1Y vs RMB900bn maturing (net −200bn); outright reverse repos +400bn net in Oct
A tidy-up, not tightening: medium-term liquidity is still up RMB200bn in October, and the overnight rate is now the policy signal.
Q3 GDP (Oct 19)
Firmer growth, near the bottom of the 4.5–5% target. It eases pressure for stimulus but was not strong enough to sell bonds.
view: Neutral leaning long for the next 1–2 weeks, with the 10-year expected in a 1.55–1.62% CCDC range. The move to a 1.25% overnight anchor is being priced as a de facto cut, the PBOC is still buying CGBs, data have softened and a wobbling equity market supports haven demand, so the drift stays lower; but the 10-year is already at a 1-year low, the curve is flat (2s10s 37bp, a 1-year low) and the PBOC keeps draining at the margin and could warn on bond risk, so gains should be slower and bumpier. I would buy the 10-year on a back-up to 1.61–1.62%, keep the 5Y-into-10Y switch, stay underweight policy banks against CGBs at 10Y and the long end, and prefer ADBC/EXIM over CDB. Hot October inflation or credit data, a sharp equity rebound or a regulator warning would push the 10-year back toward 1.62–1.63%, while weak trade or CPI data and further equity losses could take it to 1.55%.

buckets.name: CGB 1–2Y
buckets.why: The 2-year fell 0.6bp to 1.216%, a 1-year low (0th percentile, average 1.307%), and the 1-year 0.3bp to 1.168%; overnight Shibor ticked up to 1.283% as the PBOC drained for a fifth day. Funding is already priced near the 1.25% anchor, so the front end lagged the rally and has little room left.
buckets.call: Hold; add 2-year CGBs only above 1.27%, or if the overnight rate is cut below 1.25%.

buckets.name: CGB 5–7Y belly
buckets.why: 2s5s10s is −17.9bp, near the 1-year rich extreme (3rd percentile, average −7.7bp), and 5s7s10s fell 0.4bp to −9.9bp, a 1-year low. The 5s10s flattener from ~29bp is at 27.5bp (56th percentile, average 26.5bp), 1.5bp in the money and inside the 31bp stop, as the 10-year again beat the 5-year (−1.7bp vs −1.2bp).
buckets.call: Keep the 5Y-into-10Y switch (5s10s flattener) from ~29bp, target 25bp, stop 31bp.

buckets.name: CGB 10Y
buckets.why: The 10-year fell 1.7bp to 1.587%, a 1-year low and 6.3bp lower on the week, so the old 1.635–1.64% buy level now looks out of reach after the break below 1.60% and the anchor shift; I move it to 1.61–1.62%. Against neighbours it still screens cheap: 7s10s20s is −24.0bp, about the 85th percentile against a −29.4bp average.
buckets.call: Buy 10-year CGBs on a back-up to 1.61–1.62%, target 1.57%, stop 1.645%.

buckets.name: CGB 30Y
buckets.why: The 30-year fell 1.5bp to 2.027%, a 1-year low, and 10s30s is 44.1bp, about the 33rd percentile against a 45.7bp average. 30s50s at 12.5bp (8th percentile) leaves the ultra-long block little cushion, though the 50-year auction drew about 7 times cover at 2.1537%.
buckets.call: Neutral. Add above 2.10% (10s30s ~46bp); poor risk/reward below 2.05%.

buckets.name: Policy banks 2–10Y vs CGB
buckets.why: CDB 10-year widened 0.5bp to 4.9bp over CGB (16th percentile, average 9.8bp) as CGBs led the haven rally; the switch from ~3bp is about 2bp in the money. At the front end CDB 2-year is 11.7bp over CGB, still at its 1-year tight, so the trade stays at 10Y.
buckets.call: Keep the CDB 10Y into CGB 10Y switch from ~3bp, target 8bp, stop 1bp.

buckets.name: ADBC/EXIM vs CDB 10Y
buckets.why: ADBC 10-year yields 3.3bp more than CDB (76th percentile, average 1.3bp) and EXIM 2.4bp (62nd percentile, average 2.0bp); all three moved 1.2bp today. The pickup comes from heavy ADBC and EXIM tap supply rather than credit, and the taps keep clearing at or below the curve.
buckets.call: Hold ADBC/EXIM 10Y rather than CDB 10Y for the ~3bp pickup.

buckets.name: Policy banks 20–30Y
buckets.why: CDB 20-year is 4.9bp over CGB, at its 1-year low (1st percentile, average 10.6bp), and the 30-year 11.0bp, also at its 1-year tight (average 12.6bp). Long policy bank bonds again moved one for one with CGBs in the rally, leaving no spread cushion if supply picks up into year-end.
buckets.call: Prefer CGB 20–30Y to CDB 20–30Y; revisit policy bank long bonds above a 13bp 30-year spread.
